Yellow papules on erythematous base; trunk, well neonate
Resolves in days; reassure, no cultures
Bilateral nocturnal calf pain; normal exam, massage relieves
Blue hands, feet, perioral; pink mucosa, normal SpO2
Benign, first 24–48 hours; warmer if cold

obesity-and-bariatric-surgery.name: Obesity and bariatric surgery
obesity-and-bariatric-surgery.scope: Lifestyle modifications, pharmacotherapy (GLP-1 receptor agonists), indications for bariatric surgery, postoperative nutritional and surgical complications
obesity-and-bariatric-surgery.core: Chronic excess adiposity with metabolic complications; sustained treatment combines nutrition, activity, behavioral support, medications, and sometimes metabolic surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Calorie-dense diet, inactivity, sleep deprivation, genetic susceptibility, food insecurity
Glucocorticoids, antipsychotics, insulin; investigate endocrine causes when examination suggests them

rows.label: Clues
items: BMI ≥30 kg/m²; central adiposity predicts cardiometabolic risk
Screen for hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, sleep apnea, fatty liver, osteoarthritis, depression

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Adipose inflammation and insulin resistance; appetite regulation favors weight regain after weight loss
Bypass and sleeve alter gut signaling and intake; bypass additionally decreases nutrient absorption

rows.label: Dx
items: Weight trajectory, medication review, eating-disorder assessment; A1c, lipids, liver enzymes
★ Postoperative **tachycardia**, fever, abdominal pain → investigate anastomotic leak urgently

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Structured calorie deficit, activity, behavioral follow-up; **5–10% weight loss** improves metabolic disease
Child: **cut liquid calories** first (juice, excess whole milk); cause is total calorie surplus
Medications: BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with comorbidity; semaglutide or tirzepatide plus lifestyle changes
★ Avoid GLP-1 agents with **MEN 2/medullary thyroid carcinoma** history; avoid weight-loss drugs during pregnancy
★ **Surgical referral** by eligibility below; assess nutritional, operative, psychosocial readiness and lifelong follow-up

rows.label: Complications
items: Early: leak, bleeding, VTE; later: stricture, rapid-weight-loss gallstones, internal hernia with intermittent pain
Roux-en-Y: dumping after sugary meals, marginal ulcers; iron, B12, calcium, vitamin D deficiencies
Persistent vomiting → thiamine deficiency; give thiamine promptly before carbohydrate loading

rows.label: Prevention
items: Lifelong supplements and nutritional surveillance after surgery; avoid NSAIDs and tobacco after bypass
Small meals, fewer simple sugars for dumping; delay conception during rapid postoperative weight loss

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cushing syndrome: violaceous striae, proximal weakness, easy bruising
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, bradycardia; usually modest weight gain

opioid-toxicity.name: Opioid toxicity
opioid-toxicity.scope: Opioid toxidrome, naloxone administration and titration, observation period, precipitated withdrawal
opioid-toxicity.core: Depressed consciousness, slow breathing, and pinpoint pupils after opioid exposure; ventilation takes priority over full awakening.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fentanyl or heroin exposure, dose escalation, renal dysfunction, long-acting opioids
Alcohol/benzodiazepine co-ingestion; lost tolerance after detoxification, hospitalization, or incarceration

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Bradypnea or apnea** with hypoxemia; reduced bowel sounds, bradycardia, hypotension
Miosis may be absent with severe hypoxia or co-ingestion; needle marks are not required
Pulmonary edema, aspiration, hypothermia, prolonged immobilization may accompany overdose
Chronic use: daytime sleepiness, constipation, apathy, falling grades, miosis, slow breathing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mu-receptor activation suppresses medullary ventilatory response to CO2
Naloxone competitively reverses opioid effects but often wears off before the causative opioid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; bedside glucose, pulse oximetry, capnography; do not await toxicology
Urine opiate immunoassay detects morphine/heroin/codeine; may miss fentanyl, methadone, and oxycodone
ECG for methadone-associated QT prolongation; acetaminophen level with uncertain combination-product ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open airway, **bag-mask ventilation**, oxygen; intubate if ventilation cannot be maintained
★ **Naloxone** IV titrated to adequate breathing; intranasal/IM route if IV unavailable
Dependent but breathing: start low; apnea/no response: prompt larger/repeated doses, especially fentanyl analogs
Repeated recurrence → naloxone infusion; coma despite repeated doses → evaluate additional causes
Short-acting reversal: observe ≥4 hours after last naloxone; long-acting/recurrent sedation → prolonged monitoring/admission

rows.label: Complications
items: Anoxic brain injury, aspiration pneumonia, rhabdomyolysis, compartment syndrome
Precipitated withdrawal: agitation, vomiting, diarrhea, tachycardia; rare pulmonary edema after reversal

rows.label: Prevention
items: Take-home naloxone, overdose-response training, avoid sedative combinations; offer buprenorphine and addiction follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pontine hemorrhage: focal neurologic findings, no meaningful naloxone response
Clonidine poisoning: marked bradycardia with similar pupils
Sedative overdose: usually normal pupils; incomplete naloxone response

osteogenesis-imperfecta.name: Osteogenesis imperfecta
osteogenesis-imperfecta.scope: COL1A1 and COL1A2 mutations, type I collagen defect, multiple fractures, blue sclerae, dentinogenesis imperfecta, hearing loss, lethal perinatal type II
osteogenesis-imperfecta.core: Child with repeated low-impact injuries and extraosseous connective-tissue findings; variable skeletal severity can obscure the diagnosis or resemble nonaccidental trauma.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ Usually **autosomal dominant COL1A1/COL1A2 variants**; family history or de novo mutation
Unaffected parents do not exclude disease; parental germline mosaicism may cause recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Multiple fractures with minimal trauma**, ligamentous laxity, easy bruising, bone deformity
**Dentinogenesis imperfecta**: opalescent, discolored teeth with early wear or breakage
Conductive/mixed hearing loss often develops later; normal intellect

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Deficient or structurally abnormal type I collagen** impairs bone matrix and other collagen-rich tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: Skeletal radiographs: osteopenia, healed fractures, bowed bones, sometimes wormian skull bones
**Molecular genetic testing** confirms; skeletal survey assesses extent when clinically needed
Calcium, phosphate, PTH, alkaline phosphatase usually normal outside fracture healing
Assess trauma consistency, full skin examination, family history; genetic disorder and abuse can coexist

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Fracture stabilization with **brief immobilization and early rehabilitation**; avoid prolonged disuse
IV pamidronate or zoledronic acid for significant skeletal disease → improved bone density
Recurrent fractures/deformity → intramedullary rodding; physical/occupational rehabilitation and mobility aids
Dental restoration, hearing aids, and orthopedic follow-up; adequate calcium/vitamin D without megadoses

rows.label: Complications
items: Scoliosis, restrictive lung disease, chronic pain, impaired mobility; cranial involvement → basilar invagination
Bisphosphonates: acute-phase reaction, hypocalcemia; coordinate major orthopedic procedures with bone specialist

rows.label: Prevention
items: Gentle handling, safe low-impact activity, fall prevention; weight-bearing within functional limits
Genetic counseling; prenatal testing when familial variant known; periodic dental and audiology assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonaccidental trauma: inconsistent history, patterned bruises, posterior rib/metaphyseal lesions; safeguarding evaluation
Rickets: growth-plate cupping/fraying, elevated alkaline phosphatase
Hypophosphatasia: low alkaline phosphatase, premature tooth loss

table.title: Classic phenotypes
rows: Prenatal fractures; perinatal lethality, respiratory failure

ovarian-cysts.name: Ovarian cysts
ovarian-cysts.scope: Follicular cyst, corpus luteum cyst, theca lutein cyst (hyperstimulation), mature cystic teratoma (dermoid), unilocular vs multilocular, surveillance intervals, cystectomy indications, cyst rupture
ovarian-cysts.core: Most reproductive-age ovarian cysts are benign; morphology, symptoms, menopausal status, and persistence determine observation versus surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovulatory cycles, early pregnancy; ovulation induction → **hyperstimulated ovaries**; very high hCG → bilateral enlargement
Postmenopausal adnexal masses carry higher malignancy risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental mass, pelvic pressure, unilateral discomfort; sudden pain after intercourse/exertion suggests rupture
★ Sudden severe pain with vomiting → **torsion**; syncope/hypotension → major intraperitoneal bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Functional lesions arise during ovulation; dermoids contain differentiated germ-cell tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pregnancy test first; **transvaginal ultrasound** characterizes wall, septations, solid elements, flow, free fluid
Simple unilocular: thin wall, anechoic, no solid vascular component; multiloculation warrants closer characterization
Papillary/solid vascular components, thick septa, ascites → malignancy evaluation; CA-125 nonspecific premenopausally
Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; urgent clinical concern overrides reassuring imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stable functional/hemorrhagic cyst → analgesia, recheck after menses; unresolved → repeat ultrasound in **6–12 weeks**
Asymptomatic simple cyst above 5–7 cm premenopause, 3–5 cm postmenopause → ultrasound around 6–12 months
★ Hemodynamic instability → IV fluids/blood and urgent laparoscopy; torsion → detorsion with ovarian preservation
Persistent/enlarging, symptomatic, large, suspicious mass → surgery/referral
OCPs do not hasten functional-cyst resolution; older exam questions may expect OCP + 6-week recheck

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemoperitoneum, ovarian infarction, reduced ovarian reserve after surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Ovulation suppression may reduce new functional cyst formation; counsel urgent reassessment for acute pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG with pregnancy outside uterus
Tubo-ovarian abscess: fever, cervical motion tenderness, inflammatory complex mass

table.title: Cyst identities
rows: Luteal/early pregnancy; tender mass, crenulated vascular wall, hemorrhage
Bilateral multicystic ovaries; regress as hCG falls
Young; complex echogenic mass; fat, teeth, calcification

ovarian-cysts.evidence: Simple-cyst thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [SRU 2019 consensus](https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/radiol.2019191354); acute management established teaching.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones (prior postprandial biliary colic), heavy alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease
Blunt abdominal trauma + epigastric mass/raised enzymes → contrast CT for pancreatic/duodenal injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue: ↓insulin, ↓glucagon, normal insulin sensitivity; lipase may normalize

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase or amylase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT: diagnostic doubt, high fever/marked leukocytosis (necrosis?), deterioration, no improvement by 48–72 hours; not routine early
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency
Recurrent, no gallstones/alcohol → EUS or MRCP for ductal anatomy; older exam questions may expect ERCP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, reassessment, IV opioid analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** by 48 hours if tolerated; else enteral; older exam questions may expect initial bowel rest
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Uncomplicated/sterile: no antibiotics; infected necrosis: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancrelipase, fat-soluble vitamins, pain control; islet-loss diabetes → **insulin**, not sulfonylureas

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; necrosis, hemorrhage; **splenic vein thrombosis** → isolated gastric varices, normal liver
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

pediatric-neck-masses.name: Pediatric neck masses
pediatric-neck-masses.scope: Thyroglossal duct cyst, branchial cleft cyst, cystic hygroma (lymphatic malformation), congenital muscular torticollis (fibromatosis colli), cervical lymphadenitis
pediatric-neck-masses.core: Childhood neck lump: location, mobility with swallowing, tenderness, and head posture separate congenital remnants from inflammatory lymph nodes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Congenital anomalies may enlarge during URI; lymphatic malformation associated with Turner syndrome
Bacterial lymphadenitis: Staphylococcus aureus, group A Streptococcus; dental disease → oral anaerobes
Fibromatosis colli: infancy, intrauterine positioning or birth-related sternocleidomastoid injury

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Stridor, drooling, respiratory distress** → threatened airway; immediate stabilization
★ Hard, fixed, supraclavicular, enlarging mass or weight loss/night sweats → **malignancy evaluation**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Embryologic tract persistence, abnormal lymphatic channels, muscle fibrosis, or reactive/infected lymphoid tissue

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Neck ultrasound first** for superficial mass; distinguish cystic/solid lesions and detect abscess
Before midline cyst excision → confirm normally located thyroid; ectopic thyroid may be sole functioning tissue
Deep infection/airway compression → contrast CT; extensive lymphatic lesion → MRI
Persistent unexplained concerning node → excisional biopsy; CBC/differential guides hematologic evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat infection before elective congenital cyst surgery**
Toxic child, oral intolerance, or treatment failure → IV cefazolin; MRSA concern → vancomycin
Fluctuant bacterial abscess → drainage plus culture; dental source → amoxicillin-clavulanate

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent infection, abscess, airway compression; untreated torticollis → plagiocephaly and facial asymmetry

rows.label: Prevention
items: Complete tract removal reduces cyst recurrence; early positioning exercises prevent secondary deformity
Oral hygiene and dental treatment reduce odontogenic lymphadenitis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive nodes: bilateral, mobile, recent URI; usually regress with observation
Atypical mycobacteria: chronic unilateral node, violaceous skin; excision rather than routine abscess incision
Lymphoma: rubbery, persistent nodes with systemic symptoms

table.title: Location → diagnosis → treatment
rows: SCM lump; ipsilateral tilt, opposite chin

pediatric-neck-masses.evidence: Checked 2026-11-05: [CHOP neck masses](https://www.chop.edu/conditions-diseases/neck-masses); established pediatric diagnostic approach.

pertussis.name: Pertussis
pertussis.scope: Bordetella pertussis, catarrhal, paroxysmal, and convalescent stages, posttussive emesis, inspiratory whoop, macrolide therapy, postexposure prophylaxis, Tdap vaccination
pertussis.core: Prolonged paroxysmal cough with posttussive emesis; infants may present with apnea and cyanosis without a whoop.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unvaccinated/undervaccinated children, waning immunity in adolescents/adults, infected household contacts
Young infants have greatest risk of severe disease; vaccinated individuals can still transmit infection

rows.label: Clues
items: Catarrhal stage: rhinorrhea, mild cough, little or no fever; greatest early infectiousness
Inspiratory whoop often absent in adolescents/adults; convalescence can last weeks with recurrent cough
★ Infant **marked lymphocytosis**, poor feeding, or respiratory compromise; minimal fever despite serious illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: B. pertussis adheres to respiratory cilia; toxin-mediated injury impairs mucus clearance
Pertussis toxin inhibits Gi signaling; impaired lymphocyte extravasation causes circulating lymphocytosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Nasopharyngeal PCR** during first 3–4 weeks of cough; posterior nasopharynx, not throat swab
Culture most useful in first 2 weeks; late illness → validated serology when available
Treat suspected high-risk cases before results; chest imaging for respiratory compromise or suspected pneumonia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Azithromycin** preferred; TMP-SMX alternative at age ≥2 months when macrolides unsuitable
Best symptom benefit early; later treatment mainly reduces transmission within infectious window
Treat age ≥1 year within 3 weeks of cough; infants/pregnancy up to 6 weeks
Hospitalize young infants or apnea/hypoxemia; oxygen, suction, hydration and cardiorespiratory monitoring
Infant macrolides carry pyloric stenosis risk, but benefit outweighs risk; monitor vomiting

rows.label: Complications
items: Pneumonia, seizures/encephalopathy, infant pulmonary hypertension and death
Adults: rib fractures, syncope, stress incontinence from forceful coughing

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Droplet isolation until **5 days of effective antibiotics**, or 21 days from cough onset untreated
Household contacts → azithromycin prophylaxis within 21 days of index cough; also target high-risk exposures
DTaP childhood series; Tdap adolescent booster and once for adults without prior Tdap
★ **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 weeks**, preferably early in that interval

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral bronchitis: improving ordinary cough without characteristic paroxysms or epidemiologic link
Asthma: recurrent wheeze/trigger pattern, reversible airflow obstruction
Chlamydial infant pneumonia: afebrile staccato cough, eosinophilia, often prior conjunctivitis

potassium-disorders.name: Potassium disorders
potassium-disorders.scope: Hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, cardiac membrane stabilization, shift therapy, elimination
potassium-disorders.core: Potassium abnormalities can cause weakness and fatal arrhythmias; stabilize cardiac risk while identifying the cause and correcting total-body balance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hyperkalemia: AKI/CKD, RAAS blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, tissue lysis, insulin deficiency
Hypokalemia: GI losses, loop/thiazide diuretics, hyperaldosteronism, insulin/beta-agonists, magnesium depletion

rows.label: Clues
items: Flaccid weakness, paralysis, palpitations; symptoms may be absent despite dangerous levels
★ **K ≥6.5 mmol/L, ECG changes, or rapid rise** → emergency; normal ECG not reassuring
Bradycardia/high-degree AV block with renal failure → suspect hyperkalemia; calcium before pacemaker

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extracellular K changes alter membrane excitability and cardiac conduction
Acidosis/insulin deficiency shift K outward; intracellular shifts can coexist with severe total-body depletion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG + repeat potassium**, creatinine, glucose, bicarbonate, magnesium; assess drugs and acid-base status
Hemolysis, thrombocytosis/leukocytosis → pseudohyperkalemia; repeat atraumatic draw if clinically compatible
Hypokalemia: urine K distinguishes renal wasting from extrarenal loss; interpret with BP/acid-base pattern
Do not delay treatment for confirmatory blood draw when malignant ECG changes present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hyperkalemic ECG changes or dialysis-patient arrest → **IV calcium gluconate/chloride first**; protects myocardium only
★ Shift K inward: **IV insulin + dextrose**, nebulized albuterol; bicarbonate mainly with significant acidosis
Remove K: loop diuretic if urine output, selected binders; urgent dialysis for severe refractory/renal-failure cases
Mild/stable hypokalemia → oral KCl; <2.5, arrhythmia, paralysis, or no oral access → monitored IV replacement
★ **Correct magnesium deficiency** for refractory low K; never give IV potassium push; monitor glucose after insulin

rows.label: Complications
items: Ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, respiratory muscle failure
Overcorrection, rebound dyskalemia; insulin-induced hypoglycemia; IV potassium extravasation/phlebitis
Diuretic hypokalemia → **digoxin toxicity**, multifocal PVCs; check K first

rows.label: Prevention
items: Review supplements/salt substitutes; monitor K/creatinine after diuretic or RAAS-drug changes
Treat diarrhea/vomiting and underlying mineralocorticoid disorders; replace ongoing losses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Guillain-Barré: ascending areflexic weakness without explanatory electrolyte pattern
Periodic paralysis: episodic shifts, sometimes thyrotoxicosis; avoid excessive replacement causing rebound

table.title: ECG patterns
rows: Peaked T → PR prolongation → wide QRS/sine-wave
Flat T, ST depression, prominent U waves

potassium-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established electrolyte emergency principles.

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins
Immature hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis → irregular anovulatory cycles, normal for 2–3 years after menarche
Virilized boy with **prepubertal testes** → peripheral androgen, usually adrenal; central puberty enlarges testes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment
Pubertal gynecomastia, unilateral or bilateral, smooth subareolar → **reassurance**; no labs/biopsy; carcinoma very rare

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance
Normal puberty + moodiness, mild parent conflict → **puberty education** for child, parents; no drug testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up
Familial short stature: short parents, bone age matches chronologic age; constitutional delay: **delayed bone age**

table.title: Tanner staging anchors
rows: Further enlargement; menarche usually within 1–2 years

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

pulmonary-hypertension.name: Pulmonary hypertension
pulmonary-hypertension.scope: WHO groups 1-5 (PAH, left heart disease, lung disease/hypoxia, CTEPH, multifactorial), cor pulmonale, echocardiography, right heart catheterization, endothelin receptor antagonists, PDE-5 inhibitors
pulmonary-hypertension.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, syncope or right-heart failure with elevated pulmonary pressures requires hemodynamic classification before vasodilator treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Connective-tissue disease, congenital shunts, portal hypertension, HIV, methamphetamine → PAH
Left-heart disease, chronic lung disease/hypoxia or prior pulmonary embolism are common secondary contexts

rows.label: Clues
items: Loud P2, RV heave, tricuspid regurgitation murmur; exertional chest pain or presyncope
JVD, hepatomegaly and edema → right-heart failure/cor pulmonale
Severe dyspnea with relatively preserved spirometry or low DLCO suggests pulmonary vascular disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary vascular resistance or elevated left filling pressure increases RV afterload
Sustained pressure overload → RV hypertrophy, dilation, reduced output and systemic venous congestion
Chronic alveolar hypoxia (COPD, OSA) → **pulmonary vasoconstriction** and remodeling → raised vascular resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography** estimates probability and evaluates RV/left-heart function; not definitive pressure diagnosis
★ **Right-heart catheterization: mean PAP >20 mm Hg** at rest confirms PH
Precapillary: wedge ≤15 mm Hg and **PVR >2 Wood units**; postcapillary: wedge >15
★ **V/Q scan** screens CTEPH; normal perfusion essentially excludes chronic thromboembolic disease
PFT/DLCO, chest CT, sleep evaluation, HIV/autoimmune testing by history; vasoreactivity testing in selected PAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen for hypoxemia, diuresis for congestion; treat underlying disease and refer confirmed PAH/CTEPH
★ PAH → specialist **endothelin antagonist + PDE-5 inhibitor**; high-risk disease → parenteral prostacyclin
Vasoreactive idiopathic/heritable/drug-associated PAH → selected high-dose calcium-channel blocker; not empiric treatment
CTEPH → lifelong anticoagulation and pulmonary endarterectomy if operable; selected balloon angioplasty or riociguat
Do not routinely use PAH vasodilators for left-heart/lung-disease PH; PDE-5 drugs cannot combine with nitrates/riociguat

rows.label: Complications
items: RV failure, arrhythmia, syncope and death; pregnancy carries substantial maternal risk in PAH
Endothelin antagonists are teratogenic; some require liver monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid methamphetamine, address thromboembolic risk; vaccination, supervised exercise, pregnancy/contraception counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: HFpEF: elevated wedge pressure identifies postcapillary cause
Deconditioning/anemia: no catheter-confirmed pulmonary pressure elevation

renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.name: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors
renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.scope: ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, direct renin inhibitors, hyperkalemia, angioedema, cough
renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.core: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and aliskiren interrupt the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone axis at different steps.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **ACE inhibitor or ARB**: hypertension with albuminuric CKD; post-MI ventricular dysfunction
HFrEF: ACE inhibitor/ARB when sacubitril-valsartan cannot be used; aliskiren lacks outcome benefits

rows.label: Mechanism
items: ACE cleaves **C-terminal dipeptide** of angiotensin I → angiotensin II; inhibitors block this step
Efferent arteriolar dilation → ↓glomerular filtration pressure; ↓aldosterone → potassium retention

rows.label: Adverse
items: Hypotension, AKI during hypovolemia; modest stable creatinine rise expected
★ **Angioedema → stop ACE inhibitor permanently**, assess/protect airway; possible even after years

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Pregnancy**, bilateral renal artery stenosis, uncontrolled hyperkalemia
Prior ACE angioedema → no ACE inhibitor; subsequent ARB needs individualized assessment

rows.label: Interactions
items: ★ **Never combine ACE inhibitor, ARB, or aliskiren**; additive kidney injury and hyperkalemia
Potassium supplements, spironolactone, trimethoprim → ↑K; NSAID + diuretic → AKI
Sacubitril-valsartan requires **36-hour ACE inhibitor washout**; RAAS blockade can raise lithium

rows.label: Monitor
items: Baseline BP, creatinine, K → repeat within **2–4 weeks** after initiation/dose increase
Creatinine rise >30% → investigate volume depletion, NSAIDs, renovascular disease; reassess drug

rows.label: Traps
items: Advanced CKD alone → no automatic discontinuation; manage reversible hyperkalemia contributors first

salicylate-toxicity.name: Salicylate toxicity
salicylate-toxicity.scope: Aspirin overdose, mixed respiratory alkalosis and metabolic acidosis, tinnitus, hyperpyrexia, urinary alkalinization, hemodialysis indications
salicylate-toxicity.core: Aspirin exposure with tinnitus, tachypnea, fever, and a mixed respiratory alkalosis–anion-gap metabolic acidosis; normal pH can conceal severe poisoning.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intentional overdose; chronic excess aspirin or bismuth subsalicylate, especially with renal impairment
Enteric-coated preparations or bezoars → delayed peak concentrations; older adults vulnerable to chronic toxicity

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis; confusion, seizures, hypoxemia or hyperpyrexia signal severe toxicity
Children may have predominantly metabolic acidosis; chronic exposure may resemble delirium or sepsis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medullary respiratory stimulation + oxidative phosphorylation uncoupling → hyperventilation, organic acids, heat generation
Acidemia increases nonionized salicylate → CNS entry; glucose utilization rises despite normal serum glucose

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serial salicylate levels**, ABG/VBG, electrolytes/anion gap, glucose, creatinine; check acetaminophen co-ingestion
Repeat concentrations until declining with clinical improvement; one early low level cannot exclude poisoning
★ **Severity overrides the level**; falling serum concentration with worsening acidemia can reflect tissue redistribution

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway assessment, IV fluids, potassium correction; activated charcoal early if airway protected
★ **IV sodium bicarbonate** → serum/urine alkalinization; target urine pH 7.5–8; maintain potassium
★ **Hemodialysis**: altered mentation, oxygen-requiring lung injury, failed alkalinization, or pH ≤7.20
Dialyze if level >100 mg/dL; >90 mg/dL with impaired renal function; chronic toxicity needs lower thresholds
★ Intubation only if essential; **maintain hyperventilation**; neuroglycopenia → dextrose despite normal blood glucose

rows.label: Complications
items: Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, cerebral edema, renal failure, hypoglycemia, death
Sedation or inadequate ventilation → rapid acidemia and cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid aspirin for childhood viral illness; secure medications; reconcile OTC salicylate-containing products
Intentional ingestion → psychiatric assessment and suicide safety planning after medical stabilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious source; may share respiratory alkalosis and lactic acidosis
DKA: marked ketonemia and insulin deficiency; absent salicylate exposure
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap early; methanol visual injury or ethylene glycol oxalate nephropathy

salicylate-toxicity.evidence: Dialysis thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [EXTRIP salicylate recommendations](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/salicylates); other management: established toxicology teaching.

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Renal stenosis: older smoker → atherosclerotic **lipid plaque**; young/middle-aged woman → **fibromuscular dysplasia** (medial hyperplasia, renal + carotid)
Renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia + metabolic alkalosis** → aldosterone excess, primary or renovascular; normal K does not exclude it
**Abdominal bruit**, diffuse atherosclerosis, late abrupt worsening, small unilateral kidney → renal artery stenosis
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
**Episodic headache, sweating, palpitations** → pheochromocytoma; cushingoid appearance, upper-body hypertension guide testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion → juxtaglomerular **renin** → RAAS; ACE inhibitor removes efferent constriction → ↓renal flow, ↓GFR across stenosis
Autonomous aldosterone → distal sodium absorption, potassium loss, low renin; pressure natriuresis escape prevents edema
Adrenal medullary catecholamine or cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread
RA joint with new febrile monoarthritis → infection until aspirated, not flare

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight; child's hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control
★ **S aureus** most common, including RA-damaged joints: gram-positive cocci in clusters
Asplenia or recent pharyngitis → **streptococci**: gram-positive cocci in chains

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal: aspirate on **chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar** plus mucosal NAAT; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis
New warmth/effusion in OA joint → aspirate before any intra-articular steroid

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints: arthroscopic washout; **hip → operative drainage**, not serial aspiration
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection
Transient synovitis (child): afebrile, bears weight, ESR <40, WBC <12,000

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

sickle-cell-disease.name: Sickle cell disease
sickle-cell-disease.scope: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis, acute chest syndrome, splenic sequestration, aplastic crisis, stroke, sickle cell trait, hemoglobin electrophoresis
sickle-cell-disease.core: HbS polymerization causes chronic hemolysis and episodic vascular occlusion; fever, hypoxemia and focal neurologic deficits require urgent escalation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive β-globin disease; dehydration, hypoxemia, cold and infection trigger sickling
Functional asplenia → encapsulated infection from early childhood; **S. pneumoniae** leads pneumonia and fulminant sepsis

rows.label: Clues
items: Baseline anemia, reticulocytosis, jaundice; childhood dactylitis or recurrent severe bone pain
Acute chest syndrome: **new pulmonary infiltrate** plus fever, respiratory symptoms or hypoxemia
Sequestration: sudden splenomegaly, falling hemoglobin, shock; aplasia: **low reticulocyte count**, often parvovirus

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes → rigid erythrocytes, endothelial injury, ischemia and shortened RBC survival
Acute chest trigger: **infection** most common; in situ thrombosis and fat embolism less often
Severe anemia → low viscosity, vasodilation, ↓afterload → **↑cardiac output** preserves oxygen delivery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC confirms genotype; newborn screen detects disease before symptoms
Crisis → CBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin; fever → blood cultures; respiratory symptoms → chest radiograph
New focal deficit → emergency brain imaging, without delaying transfusion preparation
Distinguish osteomyelitis from infarction using cultures and MRI when focal fever/pain persists

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain crisis → prompt **IV opioid**, morphine (AKI: lower dose or hydromorphone); no meperidine; NSAID only if kidneys normal
Pain crisis support: euvolemic hydration; oxygen only for hypoxemia; no routine transfusion
★ Acute chest → oxygen, **ceftriaxone + azithromycin**, incentive spirometry; transfuse for significant anemia
Severe acute chest, stroke → **urgent exchange transfusion**; sequestration (cautious) or aplasia → simple transfusion
Fever → immediate **IV ceftriaxone/cefotaxime**, despite daily penicillin prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, avascular necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, nephropathy, retinopathy
Repeated transfusions → alloimmunization and iron overload; delayed hyperhemolysis can worsen anemia
Chronic hemolysis → ↑folate demand → **folate deficiency**, macrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hydroxyurea** raises HbF, reduces crises; monitor CBC
Penicillin prophylaxis through age 5 in HbSS; pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib and influenza vaccines
Annual transcranial Doppler ages 2–16 in HbSS/HbSβ0; abnormal → chronic transfusion program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: persistent localized pain, fever; Salmonella or S. aureus
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, no hemolytic pattern

spinal-muscular-atrophy.name: Spinal muscular atrophy
spinal-muscular-atrophy.scope: SMA type 1 (Werdnig-Hoffmann), SMA type 2, SMA type 3, SMN1 gene deletion, anterior horn cell degeneration, floppy infant, tongue fasciculations, nusinersen, onasemnogene abeparvovec
spinal-muscular-atrophy.core: Symmetric proximal weakness, hypotonia, areflexia and tongue fasciculations with preserved sensation suggest spinal muscular atrophy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive SMN1 loss, usually biallelic exon 7 deletion; carrier parents or affected siblings

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Infant: **floppy posture, weak cry/suck, paradoxical breathing**; respiratory distress may be subtle
Alertness, sensation and extraocular movements usually preserved; tremulous fingers possible
Hip dislocation, scoliosis or contractures with longer survival; progressive loss of motor abilities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Low survival motor neuron protein → anterior horn cell degeneration
More functional SMN2 copies usually soften phenotype, but copy number alone does not predict course perfectly

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SMN1 molecular testing** confirms diagnosis; sequence if deletion testing fails despite convincing phenotype
Newborn screening enables presymptomatic diagnosis; do not await overt weakness after positive screen
CK normal/mildly elevated; EMG neurogenic if diagnosis unresolved; assess swallowing and ventilation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat urgently, ideally presymptomatically**; motor neuron loss is irreversible
Intrathecal nusinersen or oral risdiplam modifies SMN2 splicing to increase functional protein
★ Eligible infants <2 years: **IV onasemnogene abeparvovec** supplies functional SMN1
Gene treatment: corticosteroids and liver/platelet monitoring; serious hepatic injury possible
Multidisciplinary respiratory support, assisted cough, feeding support, rehabilitation and orthopedic care

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, infection, aspiration, malnutrition, scoliosis; treatment changes historical survival
Nusinersen: thrombocytopenia/coagulation abnormalities and renal toxicity monitoring

rows.label: Prevention
items: Carrier screening, cascade testing, reproductive counseling; early referral after positive newborn screen
Vaccination, airway clearance and nutritional support reduce secondary morbidity

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infant botulism: constipation, acute descending weakness, ptosis/pupillary abnormalities
Duchenne dystrophy: marked CK elevation, calf pseudohypertrophy, later onset
Central hypotonia: preserved/brisk reflexes with cognitive or upper motor neuron findings

spinal-muscular-atrophy.evidence: IV gene-treatment indication checked 2026-10-30: [FDA Zolgensma](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/zolgensma); established SMA phenotypes.

syncope.name: Syncope
syncope.scope: Vasovagal / neurocardiogenic syncope, orthostatic syncope, situational syncope, cardiogenic syncope, breath-holding spells, cerebral hypoperfusion workup
syncope.core: Brief loss of consciousness from global cerebral hypoperfusion with rapid spontaneous recovery; identify cardiac danger before labeling an episode reflex-mediated.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, blood loss, autonomic dysfunction, diuretics, nitrates, alpha-1 blockers; prolonged standing, heat, fear
Structural heart disease, conduction disease, arrhythmias, family history of sudden death

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Exertional or supine syncope**, palpitations, absent prodrome, cardiac murmur → high-risk cause
Reflex prodrome: nausea, warmth, diaphoresis, tunnel vision; may include brief myoclonic jerks
Situational triggers: urination, coughing, defecation; breath-holding spells follow crying/pain in young children
Shaving, tight collar, head turning + bradycardia → **carotid sinus hypersensitivity**; confirm with carotid sinus massage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Vasodilation/bradycardia, failed postural compensation, or low cardiac output transiently limits cerebral flow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial **history, examination, orthostatic BP, ECG**; bedside glucose and targeted pregnancy/bleeding evaluation
Orthostasis: systolic fall ≥20 or diastolic ≥10 mm Hg within 3 minutes standing
High-risk → admission/monitoring; suspected structural disease → echo; intermittent arrhythmia → ambulatory ECG
Tilt-table testing for recurrent unexplained reflex/orthostatic cases; no routine head CT, EEG, carotid ultrasound
Typical breath-holding spells: normal development, awake trigger, rapid recovery; CBC/ferritin and ECG when evaluating

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reflex event → supine, legs elevated; **hydration, counterpressure maneuvers**, trigger recognition
Orthostatic cause → replace volume, review drugs, rise slowly, compression; refractory neurogenic cases → midodrine
★ Cardiac cause → **treat rhythm/obstruction**, restrict unsafe activity pending evaluation
Breath-holding: reassure caregivers, safe positioning, treat iron deficiency; no antiseizure drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, fractures, driving injury; underlying cardiac disease carries sudden-death risk
Recurrent episodes → activity limitation, anxiety; pressor drugs can cause supine hypertension

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid dehydration and prolonged immobility; individualized driving/activity restrictions after unexplained or cardiac events

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seizure: prolonged postictal confusion, lateral tongue biting; incontinence occurs in both
Hypoglycemia: persistent altered state until glucose corrected
TIA: focal deficit; isolated transient unconsciousness unusual

syncope.evidence: Not checked online; established syncope evaluation teaching.

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia.scope: Evaluation of isolated thrombocytopenia, peripheral smear, immune thrombocytopenia, drug-induced, procedural platelet thresholds
thrombocytopenia.core: Low platelet count requires confirmation and distinction among impaired production, immune destruction, consumption, sequestration, and laboratory artifact.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent infection, autoimmune disease, HIV/HCV, lymphoproliferative disease → secondary immune thrombocytopenia
Heparin, quinine, TMP-SMX, vancomycin; alcohol, marrow-suppressive drugs; cirrhosis with splenic sequestration

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gingival bleeding; mucosal hemorrhage signals clinically important platelet disorder
★ **Neurologic/renal abnormalities + hemolysis** → thrombotic microangiopathy; systemic illness/coagulopathy → DIC
Heparin exposure + >50% platelet decline, thrombosis, typical 5–10-day onset → HIT

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ITP: IgG platelet clearance, impaired megakaryocytes; maternal IgG crosses placenta → **fetal platelet destruction**
Drug-dependent immune destruction often causes abrupt severe counts; HIT: anti-PF4/heparin IgG activates platelets, producing thrombosis
**Kasabach-Merritt**: infant vascular tumor (kaposiform hemangioendothelioma/tufted angioma; older exams: hemangioma) traps platelets → severe thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Repeat CBC + peripheral smear**; platelet clumps → citrate tube for pseudothrombocytopenia
Isolated low platelets, normal coagulation, large platelets → ITP after excluding secondary causes
Schistocytes → LDH, haptoglobin, creatinine, coagulation studies; suspected TTP → urgent ADAMTS13 sample
HIV/HCV testing for new ITP; marrow biopsy only atypical cytopenias or suspected marrow disease
4Ts estimates HIT probability; intermediate/high → PF4 immunoassay, functional confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult ITP **<30,000/µL or bleeding → glucocorticoid**; children without significant bleeding → observation
★ ITP critical bleeding → **IVIG + high-dose steroid + platelet transfusion**
Drug immune thrombocytopenia → stop culprit; persistent ITP → rituximab, thrombopoietin agonist, or selected splenectomy
Suspected TTP → plasma exchange; HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban/nonheparin anticoagulant
Older board LP target: 50,000/µL; current trigger below; neurosurgical targets often ≥100,000/µL

rows.label: Complications
items: Intracranial hemorrhage with severe disease; thrombosis in HIT/TTP
Steroid toxicity, immunosuppression; splenectomy → encapsulated bacterial sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit rechallenge, aspirin/NSAIDs when bleeding risk high; vaccinate before splenectomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Von Willebrand disease: often normal platelet count with mucocutaneous bleeding
Marrow failure: additional cytopenias, abnormal precursor morphology

thrombocytopenia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AABB/ICTMG platelet recommendations (2025)](https://www.aabb.org/news-resources/news/article/2025/05/29/aabb-develops-new-platelet-transfusion-guidelines); other hematology principles not separately checked.

thrombotic-microangiopathies.name: Thrombotic microangiopathies
thrombotic-microangiopathies.scope: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (ADAMTS13, pentad, plasma exchange), hemolytic uremic syndrome (shiga toxin, supportive care), atypical HUS, schistocytes, MAHA
thrombotic-microangiopathies.core: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia plus thrombocytopenia and organ injury: urgently distinguish TTP, Shiga toxin-associated HUS, and complement-mediated HUS.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immune TTP: acquired ADAMTS13 autoantibody; autoimmune disease, pregnancy, HIV can trigger episodes
STEC-HUS: contaminated food/water, often children; recurrent episodes suggest inherited complement susceptibility
Secondary TMA: severe hypertension, pregnancy complications, transplant, calcineurin inhibitors or other drugs

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Schistocytes**, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin, reticulocytosis; direct antiglobulin test usually negative
TTP often neurologic/cardiac-predominant; HUS often renal-predominant, with substantial overlap
Classical TTP pentad: hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, fever, neurologic changes, renal dysfunction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet-rich microthrombi shear passing erythrocytes and obstruct small-vessel perfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC/smear, hemolysis studies, creatinine, urinalysis, PT/aPTT/fibrinogen; coagulation usually normal unlike DIC
★ **High PLASMIC score** supports empiric TTP management while awaiting definitive testing
ECG/troponin and neurologic examination assess otherwise occult organ injury
Normal complement levels do not exclude atypical HUS

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected immune TTP → **treat immediately**; do not await full pentad or confirmatory result
★ STEC disease: **avoid antibiotics/antimotility drugs**; RBC transfusion for symptomatic anemia
TTP: no platelets unless life-threatening bleeding; plasma infusion only if exchange unavoidably delayed

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, myocardial ischemia, seizures, renal failure, death; survivors may develop CKD or cognitive impairment
Caplacizumab → bleeding; complement inhibition → meningococcal infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: TTP remission → monitor ADAMTS13/relapse symptoms; treat marked recurrent deficiency with hematology
★ Before complement blockade: **MenACWY + MenB**; urgent start before vaccine protection → penicillin prophylaxis
Food safety and hand hygiene reduce STEC exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: DIC: prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen, systemic coagulation activation
HELLP: pregnancy-associated hypertension, elevated liver enzymes; delivery central to treatment
B12 deficiency: macrocytosis, low reticulocyte response despite striking LDH

table.title: Decisive subtype branches
rows: Urgent plasma exchange + steroids, caplacizumab, rituximab
Shiga injury; often after bloody diarrhea

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired glucose uptake + excess hepatic output; early compensatory **↑serum insulin**, later relative secretory failure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin; **lactic acidosis**: avoid eGFR <30, AKI/sepsis, hypoxia; no new start <45; reduce 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**
Otherwise GLP-1 RA before insulin; older exam questions may expect **basal insulin** once two orals fail
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain
Metformin: GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; pioglitazone: edema, HF; sulfonylureas: labeled caution with sulfa allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot and dilated eye examinations** (eye spacing by findings)
★ Albuminuria + hypertension → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**, never both; efferent dilation ↓intraglomerular pressure
BP ≥130/80 → antihypertensive; older exam questions may expect ACE inhibitor, also normotensive albuminuria
Statin age 40–75; glycemic control slows **neuropathy**, retinopathy, nephropathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

ventricular-arrhythmias.name: Ventricular arrhythmias
ventricular-arrhythmias.scope: Ventricular tachycardia (monomorphic, polymorphic/torsades de pointes), ventricular fibrillation, QT prolongation, antiarrhythmics, defibrillation and cardioversion, magnesium sulfate
ventricular-arrhythmias.core: Wide-complex tachycardia is ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise; pulse, stability, morphology, and QT determine immediate treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior MI/scar, cardiomyopathy, acute ischemia, channelopathies, myocarditis
Low K/Mg, bradycardia, congenital long QT; macrolides, antipsychotics, methadone, class IA/III antiarrhythmics

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, syncope, chest pain, dyspnea; pulseless collapse requires immediate arrest algorithm
★ **Shock, ischemia, altered mentation, acute HF** with sustained tachycardia → unstable
Torsades often follows pause-dependent long-short sequence; recurrent self-terminating runs can precede arrest
Premature **wide bizarre QRS without preceding P wave** → PVC, ventricular origin; narrow QRS with P → atrial

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Scar reentry often causes monomorphic VT; prolonged repolarization produces early afterdepolarizations and torsades
VF causes chaotic ineffective ventricular activation with no meaningful cardiac output

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Check pulse immediately**, attach monitor/defibrillator; 12-lead ECG only if stabilization not delayed
AV dissociation, capture/fusion beats, concordance favor VT over SVT with aberrancy
Measure baseline QTc, review drugs, electrolytes, ischemia; QTc >500 ms increases torsades risk
Exertional syncope or family sudden death → **12-lead ECG**: channelopathy, WPW, HCM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pulseless VT/VF → **unsynchronized defibrillation + CPR**, epinephrine; refractory shocks → amiodarone/lidocaine
★ Unstable monomorphic VT with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; sustained polymorphic VT → unsynchronized shock
Stable monomorphic VT → IV procainamide or amiodarone; avoid procainamide with prolonged QT/severe HF
★ Recurrent torsades → **IV magnesium**, stop QT drugs, replace K; acquired pause-dependent cases → overdrive pacing
Normal-QT polymorphic VT → treat ischemia, consider lidocaine/amiodarone; magnesium not routine

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiac arrest, sudden death, hypoxic brain injury, cardiogenic shock
QT-prolonging antiarrhythmics can worsen torsades; cardioversion without synchronization can induce VF in organized rhythms

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **ICD** for survivors without reversible cause; selected low-EF patients for primary prevention after optimization
Beta-blocker for chronic ischemic/structural risk; ablation for recurrent scar-related VT/ICD shocks
Correct reversible triggers; congenital long QT needs specialist beta-blocker/ICD risk assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: SVT with aberrancy: prior bundle-branch pattern; uncertainty → treat as VT
Preexcited AF: irregular very rapid wide complexes; avoid AV nodal blockers
Artifact: palpable pulse and unaffected underlying QRS despite apparent chaotic tracing
